title: Rene Louapre's arrangements and the House Rockers
summary: Working as the band supervisor's grocery boy, he received arrangements and formed his first band, the House Rockers, playing Caravan.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So who, what, did you, did you have daily, did you have daily instructions, rehearsals?
Oh, we had, you know, we had band class. Everyday band class.

Yeah. And we had instructions and we learned to therapy and reading and so forth. Because it was very, very good in, the music department in all public schools then was very, very good. I remember the band supervisor for Orleans Parish band directors was Rene Luop. Oh, that's right. Rene Luop. Yeah. It was a good thing. I, coincidence about Rene Luop, I also worked at a grocery store after school and I was Rene Luop's grocery boy. Uh-huh. I got to see him a lot more than I, a lot of the kids in the hoes, Orleans Parish, you know. Uh-huh. And he used to play for all the carnival balls and everything at Fairmont Hotel. And, uh, one day I went there and he was getting older by there and he gave me a whole basket of arrangements. I mean a grocery basket, you know, I, I, I delivered his groceries and he gave me all these arrangements. Because, uh, I had told him one time when he came to school, I said, we're going to, we're going to organize ourselves a band. And there was, uh, three of us, uh, who was in the school band and we know some guys around our house. One played drums, that was, who that was, Clifford Smith played drums, and Lil Frank played the guitar, and Mitchell played the saxophone, he had a C melody. And Rudolph August played the alto and I played the trumpet. And that was my first band called the House Rockers. So we had these arrangements, man.
And, uh, very, very, very, from your name Luab? I mean these arrangements were playing cards?

Yeah, oh yeah, yeah. We started learning how to read these things, you know. We got help from the teaching school. And, of course, our first number was Caravan. Uh huh. We had to play Caravan. That was the first number I learned how to play, other than from the school work that we played, was Caravan. So, that helped. The youngsters don't have that today.
